title: Deuteronomy Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 19.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:1, whose land does the LORD cut off for the Israelites to inherit?
options: The nations whose land the LORD giveth thee
questions.correctAnswer: The nations whose land the LORD giveth thee
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:1 states that the LORD cuts off the nations whose land He gives to Israel.

questions.question: How many cities were the Israelites commanded to separate for refuge in the midst of their land?
questions.correctAnswer: Three cities
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:2 commands the separation of three cities in the midst of the land.

questions.question: What must be prepared along with dividing the land into three parts according to Deuteronomy 19:3?
options: A way for the slayer to flee
questions.correctAnswer: A way for the slayer to flee
questions.explanation: Verse 3 instructs to prepare a way and divide the land so every slayer may flee thither.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 19:4, a slayer who killed his neighbor ignorantly and hated him before may flee to the cities for refuge.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:4 states the slayer must have killed ignorantly and must not have hated the neighbor in time past.

questions.question: In the example given in Deuteronomy 19:5, what caused the man’s neighbor to die?
options: A deliberate strike with an axe
A stroke with an axe where the head slipped from the helve
questions.correctAnswer: A stroke with an axe where the head slipped from the helve
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes a man hewing wood whose axe head slipped and struck his neighbor, causing death.

questions.question: Why was the slayer allowed to flee to one of the cities according to Deuteronomy 19:6?
options: Because he was hated by the victim
Because the avenger of blood might kill him in anger though he was not worthy of death
Because the slayer was guilty of murder
questions.correctAnswer: Because the avenger of blood might kill him in anger though he was not worthy of death
questions.explanation: Verse 6 explains the slayer flees lest the avenger kills him in hot anger, though he was not deserving of death.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 19:7 repeats the command to separate three cities for the Israelites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 7 explicitly commands again to separate three cities.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:8, what will happen if the LORD enlarges the Israelites' coast as He swore to their fathers?
options: They will lose the three cities
They will have to build a temple
They will receive all the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive all the promised land
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states that if the LORD enlarges their coast, He will give them all the promised land.

questions.question: If the Israelites keep all commandments and love the LORD, how many additional cities should be added according to Deuteronomy 19:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Three
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says they should add three more cities besides the first three if they keep all commandments.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 19:10 teaches that innocent blood should not be shed in the land given by the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 10 warns that innocent blood must not be shed in the land given by the LORD.

questions.question: Who shall fetch the man who fled into the city after killing his neighbor intentionally, according to Deuteronomy 19:12?
questions.correctAnswer: The elders of his city
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states the elders of his city shall send and fetch him to deliver him to the avenger of blood.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 19:13, pity should be shown to one who killed intentionally and fled to a city of refuge.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 13 commands not to pity him but to put away the guilt of innocent blood.

questions.question: What are Israelites forbidden to remove from their neighbor’s inheritance according to Deuteronomy 19:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Landmarks
questions.explanation: Verse 14 commands not to remove your neighbor's landmark set in inheritance.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:15, how many witnesses are required to establish a matter of sin or iniquity?
questions.correctAnswer: Two or three witnesses
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states a matter shall be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses, not one.

questions.question: If a false witness testifies against a man, what will happen to him according to Deuteronomy 19:19?
options: He will be punished as he intended for his brother
He will be made a judge
questions.correctAnswer: He will be punished as he intended for his brother
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says the false witness shall be treated as he intended to do to his brother.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:8, what condition is described concerning the enlargement of your borders?
options: The LORD will enlarge your coast if you worship other gods
The LORD will enlarge your coast as He promised to your fathers
Your borders will shrink if you keep His commandments
You must conquer new lands through war to enlarge your coast
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will enlarge your coast as He promised to your fathers
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:8 clearly states that the LORD will enlarge your coast as He has sworn to your fathers, emphasizing God's faithfulness to His promises. This ties to the covenant made with the ancestors.

questions.question: What must you do according to Deuteronomy 19:9 to be allowed to add three more cities for refuge?
options: Keep all the commandments, love the LORD, and walk in His ways
Conquer new lands with your army
Separate cities only if the population grows
questions.correctAnswer: Keep all the commandments, love the LORD, and walk in His ways
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:9 explains that adding three more cities is conditional on obedience to all commandments, loving God, and walking in His ways, highlighting faith and obedience as prerequisites.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Deuteronomy 19:10 for adding more cities of refuge?
options: So that innocent blood is not shed in the land
To increase the number of judges
questions.correctAnswer: So that innocent blood is not shed in the land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:10 states the purpose of adding cities of refuge is to prevent innocent bloodshed in the land God gives as an inheritance, emphasizing the value of justice and protection of life.

questions.question: Based on Deuteronomy 19:11, what kind of killing disqualifies a man from fleeing to a city of refuge?
options: Killing motivated by hatred and premeditation
questions.correctAnswer: Killing motivated by hatred and premeditation
questions.explanation: Verse 11 specifies that if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait, and kills him mortally, he cannot find refuge, underscoring the distinction between intentional murder and accidental killing.

questions.question: What are the elders of the city instructed to do if a murderer flees to their city according to Deuteronomy 19:12?
options: Protect him from the avenger of blood
Send and fetch him to deliver to the avenger of blood
questions.correctAnswer: Send and fetch him to deliver to the avenger of blood
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:12 commands the elders to send for the man and hand him over to the avenger of blood, demonstrating the community's role in upholding justice for intentional killers.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 19:13 instruct the community to respond emotionally to the murderer?
options: Take pity on him to avoid blood guilt
Not pity him and put away the guilt of innocent blood
questions.correctAnswer: Not pity him and put away the guilt of innocent blood
questions.explanation: Verse 13 instructs that the community should not pity the murderer but remove guilt from innocent blood, emphasizing justice over mercy in this context.

questions.question: What specific instruction does Deuteronomy 19:14 give regarding property boundaries?
options: You may move your neighbor's landmark if it benefits you
You shall not remove your neighbor's landmark set in your inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: You shall not remove your neighbor's landmark set in your inheritance
questions.explanation: The verse prohibits moving the neighbor’s boundary markers, which protects property rights and promotes integrity within the community.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:15, how many witnesses are required to establish a matter of sin or iniquity against someone?
questions.correctAnswer: Two or three witnesses
questions.explanation: Verse 15 clearly states that a single witness is insufficient; at least two or three witnesses are required to establish guilt, emphasizing fairness and due process.

questions.question: What is the consequence for a false witness according to Deuteronomy 19:19?
options: He shall be commended for bravery
He shall be punished as he intended to punish his brother
He shall be forgiven without penalty
He shall be sent to another city
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be punished as he intended to punish his brother
questions.explanation: Verse 19 mandates that a false witness receives the punishment he sought to inflict, thereby deterring false testimony and maintaining justice.

questions.question: What is the intended effect on the community when a false witness is punished, according to Deuteronomy 19:20?
options: They will fear and refrain from evil
questions.correctAnswer: They will fear and refrain from evil
questions.explanation: Verse 20 explains that the punishment of false witnesses serves as a deterrent so the community fears and avoids committing such evil acts in the future.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 19:21 summarize the principle of justice to be followed?
options: Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth
Impose harsher penalties for minor sins
questions.correctAnswer: Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth
questions.explanation: Verse 21 restates the principle of equitable justice, ensuring punishments correspond directly to the offense, emphasizing fairness and balance.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 19:10 teaches that shedding innocent blood in the land brings guilt upon the people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 10 warns that innocent bloodshed in the land given by God brings guilt upon the people, emphasizing the seriousness of protecting innocent life.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 19:14, it is permissible to move your neighbor's boundary markers if it benefits your inheritance.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 14 expressly forbids removing a neighbor’s landmark, protecting fairness and respect for others' property rights.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 19:9 suggests that obedience and love for God lead to an increase in cities of refuge.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 9 connects faithful obedience and love for God to the blessing of adding three more cities of refuge, showing the link between obedience and God’s provision.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 19:9-10 together teach about the importance of obedience in relation to community safety?
options: Obedience is unrelated to community safety
Obedience leads to more cities of refuge to prevent innocent bloodshed
Obedience leads to fewer cities to control population
Obedience allows shedding innocent blood without guilt
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience leads to more cities of refuge to prevent innocent bloodshed
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 together show that keeping commandments and loving God results in the establishment of more refuge cities, which help prevent innocent bloodshed and protect the community.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 19.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:15, how many witnesses are required to establish a matter against a man for any sin?
questions.correctAnswer: Two or three witnesses
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:15 states that 'at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established,' emphasizing the need for multiple witnesses to confirm a claim.

questions.question: What is the prescribed action if a false witness is found to have testified falsely against his brother?
options: The false witness shall be forgiven
The false witness shall be punished as he intended for his brother
The false witness shall be exiled
The false witness shall pay a fine
questions.correctAnswer: The false witness shall be punished as he intended for his brother
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:19 prescribes that the punishment for a false witness is to do unto him as he had thought to do unto his brother, thus removing evil from among the people.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 19:21, what principle of justice is emphasized?
options: Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth
questions.correctAnswer: Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:21 clearly states the lex talionis principle: 'life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth,' emphasizing equitable retribution in justice.

questions.question: What role do the priests and judges play when a controversy arises between two men according to Deuteronomy 19:17?
options: They judge and investigate the matter before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They judge and investigate the matter before the LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:17 states that the men shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and judges, who will make an inquiry, showing their judicial role in resolving disputes.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 19:14 instructs not to remove a neighbor's landmark. What is the significance of this in the historical and cultural context of ancient Israel?
options: It prevents theft of land and maintains tribal boundaries
It encourages expansion of personal property
It forbids building on neighbor's land
It promotes communal ownership of land
questions.correctAnswer: It prevents theft of land and maintains tribal boundaries
questions.explanation: In ancient Israel, landmarks marked property boundaries; removing them was akin to stealing land, so Deuteronomy 19:14 prohibits this to protect inheritance and social order.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'avenger of blood' in Deuteronomy 19:6?
options: A family member seeking justice for a slain relative
questions.correctAnswer: A family member seeking justice for a slain relative
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'goel hadam' refers to a kinsman who avenges blood, usually a close relative who seeks justice for murder, as described in Deuteronomy 19:6.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:11-13, what must be done to a man who hates his neighbor, lies in wait, and kills him intentionally and flees to a city of refuge?
options: He must be protected and allowed to live
The elders must deliver him to the avenger of blood to be put to death
He must be exiled for life
questions.correctAnswer: The elders must deliver him to the avenger of blood to be put to death
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 instruct that intentional murderers who flee to cities of refuge are to be handed over to the avenger of blood for execution, removing innocent blood guilt from Israel.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 19:20 suggest the community should respond after a false witness has been punished?
options: They should fear and avoid committing such evil again
They should seek revenge on the family of the false witness
questions.correctAnswer: They should fear and avoid committing such evil again
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:20 states that those who remain shall hear, fear, and henceforth refrain from such evil, indicating a deterrent effect on the community.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the principle of requiring multiple witnesses as stated in Deuteronomy 19:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 18:16
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:16 reiterates the requirement of two or three witnesses to establish a matter, reflecting the legal principle found in Deuteronomy 19:15.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 19:21 with the phrase 'life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth'?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The repetition and balanced structure of 'life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth' in Deuteronomy 19:21 exemplifies parallelism, a common poetic device in Hebrew literature.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 19:16-18 requires judges to thoroughly investigate accusations before condemning anyone.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 16-18 describe the judges making a diligent inquiry to verify if a witness is false, underscoring the requirement for thorough investigation before judgment.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 19:10, the establishment of cities of refuge is to allow intentional murderers to escape justice.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:10 states cities of refuge are to prevent innocent bloodshed, implying protection for unintentional killers, not intentional murderers who deserve death.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:8-9, under what condition are three additional cities of refuge to be added?
options: If the LORD enlarges the territory and the people keep His commandments
If the elders decide to expand
questions.correctAnswer: If the LORD enlarges the territory and the people keep His commandments
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 command adding three more cities if God enlarges the land and the people obey His commandments, showing a link between obedience and provision.

questions.question: How does the principle of 'eye for eye' in Deuteronomy 19:21 relate to the New Testament teaching in Matthew 5:38-39?
options: Matthew teaches to turn the other cheek, contrasting with Deuteronomy's retributive justice
Matthew repeats Deuteronomy's law without change
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew teaches to turn the other cheek, contrasting with Deuteronomy's retributive justice
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:38-39 contrasts Deuteronomy 19:21 by instructing forgiveness and non-retaliation, showing a development from Old Testament law to New Testament ethics.

questions.question: What is the authorial intent behind the command in Deuteronomy 19:13 to not pity the murderer but remove guilt from Israel?
options: To ensure justice and prevent innocent blood guilt in the community
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure justice and prevent innocent blood guilt in the community
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:13 commands removing guilt of innocent blood to maintain communal holiness and justice, reflecting God's standard for Israel's society.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the command to establish three cities of refuge in the land given by God?
options: God's justice in protecting the innocent
God's mercy in providing a place for the slayer to flee
God's omniscience in foreseeing all sins
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy in providing a place for the slayer to flee
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:2 explains the establishment of three cities of refuge so that the slayer who killed unintentionally might find safety. This reveals God's mercy in providing protection for those not guilty of intentional murder.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 19:4, what is the condition of the person who may flee to the cities of refuge to live?
options: One who killed his neighbor intentionally after a dispute
One who killed his neighbor ignorantly and hated him not in time past
One who stole from his neighbor and repented
One who falsely accused his neighbor of sin
questions.correctAnswer: One who killed his neighbor ignorantly and hated him not in time past
questions.explanation: Verse 4 specifies that the slayer who killed his neighbor ignorantly, without prior hatred, may flee to these cities. This distinguishes unintentional from intentional killing.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught by the provision that the avenger of blood must not kill the slayer before trial, as stated in Deuteronomy 19:6?
options: The doctrine of due process and justice
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of due process and justice
questions.explanation: Verse 6 warns against the avenger killing the slayer rashly, teaching the importance of due process and justice before punishment, reflecting God's righteous judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is drawn from Deuteronomy 19:9 and 19:10 regarding obedience and the establishment of cities of refuge?
options: Obedience to God leads to territorial expansion and requires more cities to prevent innocent bloodshed
Expansion of land is guaranteed regardless of obedience
Cities of refuge are symbolic and not literal
Obedience is unrelated to the number of cities
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God leads to territorial expansion and requires more cities to prevent innocent bloodshed
questions.explanation: Verse 9 links obedience to God's commandments with the enlargement of territory and the need to add three more cities, while verse 10 emphasizes preventing innocent bloodshed on the land God gives, showing the connection between holiness and justice.

questions.question: Which aspect of God's character is revealed in the command to put away false witnesses as described in Deuteronomy 19:18-19?
options: God's holiness and demand for truth
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and demand for truth
questions.explanation: Verses 18-19 describe the judges' duty to remove false witnesses, reflecting God's holiness and intolerance of deceit to maintain justice.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 19:14 contribute to the biblical theology of covenant and inheritance?
options: It forbids removing neighbor's landmarks, upholding covenantal boundaries and land inheritance
It encourages expanding boundaries by any means
It teaches that inheritance is spiritual only
It permits changing landmarks to suit personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: It forbids removing neighbor's landmarks, upholding covenantal boundaries and land inheritance
questions.explanation: Verse 14 forbids moving landmarks set by ancestors, emphasizing respect for God-ordained land inheritance and covenantal order.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative function do the cities of refuge serve in Deuteronomy 19:1-7?
options: They prefigure Christ as the ultimate refuge and mediator for sinners
They establish a purely civil legal system without spiritual significance
They foreshadow the destruction of Israel's enemies
They symbolize the exile of Israel from the land
questions.correctAnswer: They prefigure Christ as the ultimate refuge and mediator for sinners
questions.explanation: The cities of refuge provide protection for the innocent slayer, typologically pointing to Christ who offers ultimate sanctuary and mediates salvation for sinners (cf. Hebrews 6:18-20).

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 19:11-13 teach about the nature of justice regarding intentional murder?
options: Intentional murderers must be handed over to the avenger of blood without pity
All murderers are forgiven if they flee to cities of refuge
Intentional murder is tolerated if done in self-defense
questions.correctAnswer: Intentional murderers must be handed over to the avenger of blood without pity
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 command that those who hate and kill deliberately are not protected but are to be delivered to the avenger for execution, showing God's demand for justice against willful sin.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the principle of 'life for life, eye for eye' in Deuteronomy 19:21?
options: The doctrine of grace and forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of just retribution
questions.explanation: Verse 21 teaches the principle of lex talionis, reflecting God's righteous demand for proportionate punishment as a basis for justice in society.

questions.question: What theological synthesis arises from combining the instructions about false witnesses in verses 15-21 with the cities of refuge in verses 1-10?
options: God's justice requires both protection for the innocent and punishment for the guilty through fair testimony and refuge
Cities of refuge are a safeguard against false witnesses only
False witnesses can find refuge in the cities if repentant
The legal system is irrelevant to divine justice
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice requires both protection for the innocent and punishment for the guilty through fair testimony and refuge
questions.explanation: Verses 1-10 establish protection for innocent slayers, while verses 15-21 emphasize truthful testimony and punishment for false witnesses, together showing God's comprehensive justice system.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 19:8-10 relate the expansion of Israel's borders to moral responsibility?
options: God promises territorial increase contingent upon obedience and the prevention of innocent bloodshed
Territorial increase occurs regardless of Israel's moral conduct
Moral responsibility is unrelated to land possession
Expansion guarantees exemption from God's laws
questions.correctAnswer: God promises territorial increase contingent upon obedience and the prevention of innocent bloodshed
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 link God's oath to enlarge Israel's borders with Israel's obedience and the establishment of more cities to protect innocent blood, indicating moral accountability.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Old Testament laws on 'eye for eye' promote excessive vengeance. What does Deuteronomy 19:21 actually teach about this law?
options: It teaches proportional justice, limiting retaliation to equal harm
It permits punishment beyond the offense
It abolishes all forms of punishment
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches proportional justice, limiting retaliation to equal harm
questions.explanation: Verse 21 sets a principle of exact retribution, preventing excessive vengeance and ensuring fairness, consistent with God's justice (cf. Leviticus 24:20).

questions.question: What does the instruction in Deuteronomy 19:15 about requiring two or three witnesses reveal about God's standard for justice?
options: God demands multiple witnesses to establish truth and prevent false accusations
One witness is sufficient for conviction
Witnesses are not necessary in God's justice
Justice is based on majority opinion
questions.correctAnswer: God demands multiple witnesses to establish truth and prevent false accusations
questions.explanation: Verse 15 requires at least two or three witnesses to confirm a charge, reflecting God's high standard for truth and the protection of the innocent.

questions.question: Combining Deuteronomy 19:16-20, what is the intended social effect of punishing false witnesses harshly?
options: To deter false testimony and promote communal fear of sin
To allow false witnesses to repent freely
To ignore false testimony as unimportant
questions.correctAnswer: To deter false testimony and promote communal fear of sin
questions.explanation: Verses 16-20 explain that punishing false witnesses removes evil and causes the people to fear, leading to less wickedness in the community.

questions.question: What does the command in Deuteronomy 19:13 that the community must not pity the intentional murderer teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: God's justice demands impartiality and removal of guilt to maintain holiness
God's holiness allows for exceptions in judgment
Pity should override justice in all cases
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice demands impartiality and removal of guilt to maintain holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 13 commands the community to avoid pitying the murderer, emphasizing the necessity of impartial justice to remove guilt and uphold holiness.
